title: 97% of People Search Online Before Choosing a Local Business

segments.text: 97% of people search online before choosing a local business. If your site is slow or incomplete, that traffic goes to whoever isn't.
76% Visit Within 24 Hours of a Local Search
segments.narration: 76 percent of people who find a local business on their phone visit within 24 hours. 28 percent make a purchase from that search. The window between someone finding you online and walking through your door is less than a day.

When a page takes five seconds to load, 90 percent of visitors leave before seeing anything. At one second, only 9 percent leave. That's not a technical problem — it's a revenue leak hiding in plain sight.

The average service business saves 4.5 hours per week by switching to online booking alone. Stacked with automated follow-up emails, digital intake forms, and online payments, that compounds to 10 to 15 hours per week — 13 to 20 thousand dollars annually in labor costs.

segments.title: How Customers Research Before Choosing a Local Business
segments.narration: Online search leads by a massive margin — 97 percent. Word of mouth and social media trail at 55 and 44 percent — and both of those eventually send people to a Google search or directly to your website. If that destination is a weak page, all the goodwill from referrals evaporates.
